title: Consumer Protection Ordinance (Ordinance 37 of 2016, Cap. 17.14), ss.33-35: misleading, deceptive or unconscionable conduct and false or misleading representations
citation: Consumer Protection Ordinance, Ordinance 37 of 2016 (Cap. 17.14), revised edition showing the law as at 31 March 2021, as amended by Ordinance 22 of 2019
evidence: Revised edition front matter and Commencement note (opened 2026-11-10): "Ordinance 37 of 2016 .. in force 7 December 2019 (L.N. 48/2019)" and "Amended by Ordinance: 22 of 2019 .. in force 24 February 2020 (L.N 4/2020)"; Commencement [7 December 2019]. Section 35(1): "A person shall not, in the course of trade or business in connection with the supply or possible supply of goods or services or with the promotion by any means of the supply or use of goods or services make a false or misleading representation"; section 33(1)(a): "A person shall not, in the course of trade or business— (a) engage in conduct that is misleading or deceptive or is likely to mislead or deceive".

Only the revised edition as at 31 March 2021 is served; the annual page 2016 lists the as-enacted Ordinance 37 of 2016 and 2019 lists Ordinance 22 of 2019. English only; no government translation exists because English is the official language. Sections 33 to 35 are general misleading-conduct offences for traders; none mentions environmental or sustainability claims.
